name: Platform-Neutral Authentication Standards
consequences: Adopting open standards like FIDO2/WebAuthn reduces reliance on proprietary OS signals but requires rearchitecting trust models that currently depend on platform-specific telemetry. This shifts friction from technical implementation to institutional adoption, as legacy systems and procurement policies remain aligned with incumbent vendors.
options: Implement FIDO2-based authentication with browser-verified device integrity checks
Develop a national standard for platform-neutral cryptographic attestation
Pilot hardware-token-based authentication independent of OS app stores
review: Prioritizing open standards risks underestimating institutional resistance to reconfiguring legacy systems, leaving the gap of how to retrofit existing public-sector applications without disrupting service continuity.

name: Procurement Mandate Enforcement
consequences: Instituting mandatory compliance clauses for platform neutrality in public-sector contracts forces vendors to adapt but creates immediate compliance costs for existing systems reliant on Apple/Google infrastructure. This could slow adoption if procurement processes lack capacity to evaluate alternatives.
options: Require all digital identity contracts to include platform-neutral access clauses
Establish a phased compliance timeline with technical transition support
Create a third-party audit mechanism for procurement adherence
review: Mandating compliance risks overwhelming procurement offices without dedicated support structures, leaving the gap of how to scale technical capacity across decentralized public-sector agencies.

name: Coalition-Driven Policy Advocacy
consequences: Building cross-sector coalitions amplifies policy influence but introduces coordination challenges as stakeholders prioritize different outcomes, from privacy to operational efficiency. This could dilute the project's technical focus if advocacy efforts diverge from core resilience goals.
options: Launch multi-stakeholder forums to co-design fallback authentication requirements
Leverage EU eIDAS2 working groups to align national standards with European resilience mandates
Establish a citizen-led oversight board for digital identity continuity planning
review: Coalition-building risks fragmenting advocacy efforts across competing interests, leaving the gap of how to maintain technical coherence amid diverse stakeholder priorities.

name: Technical Demonstrator Prioritization

This could limit the scope of fallback models explored if stakeholders demand premature deployment.
options: Develop a FIDO2-based demonstrator for public-sector identity providers
Create a browser-agnostic authentication flow using WebAuthn and open-source frameworks
Build a hardware-token prototype with minimal OS dependencies
review: Prioritizing demonstrator utility risks narrowing the scope of technical exploration, leaving the gap of how to address edge cases in heterogeneous digital identity ecosystems.

name: Regulatory Sandboxing for Alternatives
consequences: Creating regulatory exceptions for alternative authentication methods accelerates innovation but introduces compliance risks if sandboxed solutions fail to meet existing security standards. This could delay adoption if regulators perceive non-conformant models as insufficiently vetted.
options: Designate a controlled environment for testing platform-neutral authentication protocols
Collaborate with regulators to update security benchmarks for alternative systems
Use existing EU Digital Identity Wallet frameworks as a compliance baseline
review: Sandboxing introduces regulatory uncertainty that could deter stakeholder participation, leaving the gap of how to transition from experimental models to production-grade implementations.

options: Certify alternative authentication providers with equivalent security guarantees
Implement dynamic supplier rotation based on real-time risk assessments
Develop a centralized trust registry for non-platform authentication services
review: Diversification risks creating fragmented trust ecosystems, leaving the gap of how to ensure interoperability between competing authentication providers.

options: Establish joint continuity planning with certified private identity providers
Create a public-private fund for fallback authentication development

review: Public-private partnerships risk prioritizing commercial interests over public accountability, leaving the gap of how to enforce transparency in third-party authentication arrangements.
